>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
President Trump's special envoy, Steve Whitcoff,
has arrived in St. Petersburg for talks
with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The focus of their meeting is expected
to be Russia's war with Ukraine.
Whitcoff met yesterday with Ukraine's president,
Volodymyr Zelensky, in Norway.
NPR's Emily Fang says Trump continues to call for Kiev
to make a deal with Moscow to end the war.
>> Trump said the US had spent billions
in sending aid to Ukraine, and for what, he asked.
He also cited high casualty figures
in the tens of thousands a month in the Russia-Ukraine war,
noting Russia is a far bigger country.
>> They have a lot of people to draw from.
Ukraine does not have a lot of people to draw from.
And it's time to make a deal.
>> Ukraine Zelensky has been lobbying US officials
from both parties and said
that the US military intelligence sharing
had been restored after it was paused for days.
But he says the US is still delaying the delivery
of American Patriot missiles to Ukraine
and argues the US's recent announcement
to purchase Russian diesel fuel further empowers Moscow.
Emily Fang and Pir News, the White House.
>> President Trump and Vice President Vance
are promoting a new effort to crack down on suspected fraud
in the federal government.
It's called the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program.
It encourages people to report suspected fraud.
Tips that lead to a conviction
or a significant federal enforcement action
are eligible for payments of up to $30,000.
Here's the president speaking at the White House.
>> All Americans will now be able to go to the fraud.gov
and report cases of corruption
and theft of taxpayer dollars in their communities,
all via a new website.
The program will be administered by the Justice Department.
The state of Florida has executed its 18th
death row inmate this year.
77-year-old William Reeves was put to death
by lethal injection for killing a sheriff's deputy
back in 1986.
Regan McCarthy with member station WFSU
reports from Tallahassee.
>> A vigil outside the governor's mansion
took place at the same time Reeves was put to death.
Peter Cowdery was among the group.
We are here hoping and praying
that there'll be an end to all of this.
We don't understand the cadence of killing that we see
and this march of death that is weekly
or something close to it, sometimes twice in one day.
It makes no sense.
>> Florida is on pace to pass its record set last year
of 19 executions.
That comes as lethal injection is facing increased scrutiny,
following a failed execution in Tennessee.
Unlike that state, Florida uses a three-drug protocol.
For NPR News, I'm Regan McCarthy in Tallahassee.
>> Wall Street futures are mostly higher this morning.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Alabama's Governor Kay Ivey says she's commuting
the death sentence of an inmate on that state's death row.
DeForest Johnson will now serve life in prison
without the possibility of parole
after the district attorney and others raised doubts
about his guilt.
Federal regulators have approved
the Boeing 737 MAX 10 jet for commercial service.
NPR's Joel Rose says this latest MAX aircraft
went through years of certification delays.
>> The Federal Aviation Administration says
it has approved the largest version
of Boeing's best-selling 737 line
after extensive safety reviews
and thousands of hours of test flights.
At one point, Boeing expected to begin delivering
the MAX 10 by 2023, but the company faced
a more stringent certification process
after two fatal crashes of the smaller MAX 8 model
in 2018 and 2019.
Boeing now expects to start delivering the MAX 10 next year
and says it has a lengthy backlog of orders
from airlines around the world.
The certification is the latest sign
of growing confidence in Boeing from U.S. regulators.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
>> SpaceX is reporting a sharp jump in quarterly earnings
that far surpassed Wall Street expectations.
The company says revenue in the third quarter
was up 161%.
It came in at more than $14.5 billion.
SpaceX cites its artificial intelligence business,
which it says expanded ninefold during the term.
SpaceX reported the earnings numbers
after yesterday's closing bell on Wall Street.
The company's shares are higher in premarket trading.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News in Washington.
